purpose: Clindamycin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections such as skin infections, lung infections, bone and joint infections, and pelvic infections. It is also sometimes used to treat certain dental infections and can be applied to the skin to treat acne. Your doctor prescribed it because it is effective against the specific type of bacteria causing your infection.
how_it_works: Clindamycin works by stopping bacteria from making the proteins they need to grow and multiply. Think of it like cutting off the bacteria's food supply — without those proteins, the bacteria cannot survive or spread. This gives your immune system the chance it needs to clear the infection from your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, and diarrhea. Some people may notice a metallic taste in their mouth. If you are using the topical form for skin or acne, you might experience mild skin dryness, redness, or irritation at the application site.
warnings: Important: Contact your doctor right away if you develop severe or persistent diarrhea, bloody stools, or stomach cramps during or even weeks after finishing treatment — this could be a serious gut infection called C. difficile. Tell your doctor if you have a history of colitis or bowel disease. Allergic reactions are rare but serious — seek emergency help if you develop rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing. Do not share this medication with others.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual oral dose is 150 to 450 mg taken every 6 hours (4 times a day), depending on the severity of the infection. Always take it with a full glass of water to help prevent throat irritation. Complete the entire course of antibiotics even if you feel better early — stopping too soon can allow the infection to come back.
